teaser.text: Nike, Inc. is a global brand company that designs and sells products for sport and everyday life. It turns footwear, apparel, equipment, and trademarks into sales through its own channels and through retail partners.

stock.title: Nike stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Nike's stock forecast weighs a difficult first year against recovery, with demand, pricing and cash conversion as the hinge.
stock.opening: Nike's weighted forecast falls to $24.62 in October 2027 and reaches $45.27 in October 2029; bear, base and bull probabilities are 32%, 50% and 18%. It hinges on renewed demand, healthier prices and stronger cash conversion.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Nike's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Nike's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: Nike’s weighted forecast falls to $24.62 in October 2027 and reaches $45.27 in October 2029; the path hinges on renewed demand, healthier prices and stronger cash conversion. Management guides to adjusted diluted EPS of $1.15 to $1.35 for the year to May 2027, with $300 million of Pace-related pre-tax charges. It expects a high-single-digit revenue decline in FY27 and a 400-basis-point headwind in the quarter to November 2026. Pace—Nike’s cost-cutting and simplification program—targets about $2.5 billion of cumulative savings through FY31 before reinvestment. Those savings must outweigh transition costs and weaker sales.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Nike's stock forecast?

paragraphs.text: The forecast implies a 29% loss including dividends by October 2027, then a 36% gain by October 2029, from $37.13 today. Bear, base and bull probabilities are 32%, 50% and 18%. Full-price sell-through, healthier retailer reorders and less reliance on markdowns are decisive. The October 2026 “made for China” collection and November Investor Day test local execution and the recovery plan. Nike’s upside requires demand and cash conversion to return before savings can support margins and buybacks.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Nike really make?

paragraphs.text: Cash from operations measures cash generated by the business; free cash flow subtracts spending on stores, distribution, technology and equipment. Stock compensation is deducted in the briefing’s “real free cash flow” measure because awards do not use cash immediately but can dilute owners over time.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Nike today?

paragraphs.text: Trailing P/E uses the last twelve months of earnings, while forward P/E uses expected earnings. Nike said FY26 earnings per share would have been $1.58 without tariff recovery. That temporary benefit makes recent earnings look stronger, so a higher forward P/E warns that near-term earnings may fall before they recover.

blocks.heading: How much does Nike pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The base dividend rises from $1.63 to $1.84 per share. The bear case freezes it at $1.63, while the bull case reaches $2.16. The freeze is credible because FY26 free cash flow of $2.184 billion was below dividends paid of $2.407 billion. The balance sheet's $9.027 billion of cash and short-term investments supports a freeze rather than an immediate cut.

blocks.heading: Does Nike's dividend fit its free cash flow?

paragraphs.text: Over the five fiscal years shown, shareholder payouts exceeded free cash flow in several years, and net cash declined across the period. That does not prove Nike could not afford the payments. Free cash flow is a flow during one year, while cash and investments on the balance sheet are a stock accumulated over earlier years. But repeated shortfalls reduce the cushion available for inventory, restructuring and new investment.

paragraphs.text: By October 2027, the bear view strengthens if China and weak franchises continue to decline, while adjusted EPS falls outside management's $1.15-to-$1.35 range. It weakens if inventory clearance produces full-price demand and margins stabilize.

By October 2028, the bull view gains support if performance products create repeat demand, China and wholesale execution recover, and revenue growth broadens. By October 2029, lower markdowns, Pace savings and stronger cash conversion must lift margins and fund buybacks; otherwise the restrained base multiple remains appropriate.

blocks.heading: What is Nike's dividend yield against its price?

paragraphs.text: Revenue peaked in May 2024. Operating margin was 8.2% in May 2026, while Nike’s own real free cash flow was 3.2% of revenue. Real free cash flow had been 11.3% of revenue in May 2024, and real free cash flow per share was $0.99 in May 2026. At $37.13, shares trade at 17.9x trailing and 24.8x next-twelve-month earnings. The free-cash-flow yield is 4.0%, and the real free-cash-flow yield is 2.7%. Payouts exceeded free cash flow in May 2026, while buybacks were $146 million.

blocks.heading: What do Nike's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Nike also beat quarterly earnings expectations in each of the eight quarters shown from Q2 fiscal 2025 through Q1 fiscal 2027. Revenue beat in seven of those quarters. That record shows that Nike can outperform a quarterly estimate, but it does not settle the larger question. A company can beat a lowered quarterly bar while guiding to a weak year, so the analyst yardstick must now focus on demand, prices and cash.

blocks.heading: What should Nike watch in the next release?

paragraphs.text: The turnaround will be credible only if Nike converts strategy and restructuring into full-price demand and steadier cash.

The first signs are operational. Investors should watch whether legacy footwear supply declines, digital sales recover at full price, and wholesale relationships improve without simply shifting discounted goods into stores. Performance sports have shown momentum, but Sportswear, Jordan Brand and Greater China still need corrective work. A rebound in one sport would not prove that the whole company has recovered.
